body:
`patch_inplace()` built its error messages inline. In particular, `get_value()` concatenated the context-sensitive `operation 'x'` string on **every** call, even when the member was present. This PR moves the JSON Patch exceptions out of line:

- **Index and key errors** reuse `basic_json`'s existing `throw_array_index_out_of_range` and `throw_key_not_found` from #5838.
- **The seven patch-specific messages** each get one `NEVER_INLINE` helper in `detail/exceptions.hpp`: add/remove parent not a container, not an array, missing member, move into child, test failed, invalid operation.
- **`get_value()`** now builds the `operation 'x'` string only inside the missing-member helper.

Exception ids and messages are byte-identical. `unit-throw_messages` gets a `patch` section that pins all 14 messages. It strips the `(/0) ` prefix that `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` adds, so the section passes in both configurations.

## Measured

`patch(diff(a, b))` on citm_catalog, best of 9, alternating builds:

| Compiler | Before (#5839) | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apple clang, `-O2` | 2.03–2.07 ms | 1.89–1.96 ms | −6.6 % |
| GCC 16, `-O2` | 3.04–3.10 ms | 2.75–2.79 ms | −9.5 % |

The GCC numbers come from the all-sites prototype, before it was reduced to the patch sites.

## Deliberately left inline

The other exceptions that are still built inline were prototyped together and measured on parse, accept, dump, all binary writers and diff for citm, twitter and canada. Nothing moved beyond noise: ±2.8 % on clang, ±1.5 % on GCC. These sites stay as they are, because they are cold or already behind a call:

- `parser::syntax_error`
- 9 sites in `binary_writer` and `throw_on_discarded`
- the two invalid UTF-8 sites in `serializer`
- `input_adapters`' empty input
- `to_json`'s `enum_key_duplicate`
- `format_error` (std::format parsing)

## Performance summary of stack #5841

The table compares the top of the stack (this PR, which contains all eleven PRs) with `develop` (4e294f4b1).
- Every row is the best of 3 alternating rounds, and each round already takes the best of 5–15 repetitions.
- Compilers: Apple clang 21 (`-O2 -DNDEBUG`, arm64) and GCC 16 (`-O2 -DNDEBUG`, Docker on the same machine).
- Documents: nativejson-benchmark's citm_catalog, twitter and canada.

| PR | Operation | clang: develop → stack | GCC 16: develop → stack |
|---|---|---|---|
| #5834 | `ordered_json::flatten()` citm | 257 → 2.4 ms (**−99 %**) | 264 → 3.7 ms (**−99 %**) |
| #5834 | `json::flatten()` citm | 5.49 → 4.82 ms (−12 %) | 7.82 → 6.88 ms (−12 %) |
| #5836 | `json_pointer(string)` | 199 → 101 ns (−49 %) | 286 → 136 ns (−52 %) |
| #5836 | `json_pointer::to_string()` | 243 → 111 ns (−54 %) | 380 → 82 ns (−78 %) |
| #5836 | `at(json_pointer)` | 77 → 58 ns (−25 %) | 123 → 75 ns (−39 %) |
| #5836 | `contains(json_pointer)` | 102 → 54 ns (−47 %) | 160 → 75 ns (−53 %) |
| #5836 | `unflatten()` citm | 21.8 → 13.3 ms (−39 %) | 32.7 → 20.0 ms (−39 %) |
| #5833 | `get<std::vector<int>>`, per element | 4.45 → 0.95 ns (−79 %) | 1.55 → 0.96 ns (−38 %) |
| #5833 | canada `get<vector<vector<vector<double>>>>` | 1.96 → 1.32 ms (−33 %) | 1.53 → 1.47 ms (−4 %) |
| #5837 | `json(std::move(vector<string>))`, 200k | 14.3 → 9.2 ms (−36 %) | 22.0 → 10.7 ms (−51 %) |
| #5832 | `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`: `ordered_json` 100k `push_back` | 1564 → 1.5 ms (**−99.9 %**) | 1643 → 1.1 ms (**−99.9 %**) |
| #5832 | `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`: `ordered_json::update()`, 20k keys | 765 → 582 ms (−24 %) ¹ | 773 → 544 ms (−30 %) ¹ |
| #5832 | `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS`: copy citm | 1.73 → 1.56 ms (−10 %) | 2.98 → 2.51 ms (−16 %) |
| #5840 | copy a scalar `json` | 2.88 → 0.95 ns (−67 %) | 2.88 → 1.92 ns (−33 %) |
| #5840 | `j == 5` | 3.52 → 0.64 ns (−82 %) | 2.88 → 1.91 ns (−34 %) |
| #5840 | `std::vector<json>` of 1M ints, build + destroy | 2.52 → 2.24 ms (−12 %) | 1.06 → 0.93 ms (−12 %) |
| #5840 | canada `==` canada | 0.52 → 0.31 ms (−40 %) | 0.52 → 0.50 ms (−4 %) |
| #5840 / #5835 | copy canada | 3.08 → 2.94 ms (−5 %) | 4.25 → 3.78 ms (−11 %) |
| #5838 | `get_ref<const std::string&>()` | 1.16 → 0.32 ns (−73 %) | 0.32 → 0.32 ns (±0) |
| #5838 | `at(i)` | 1.31 → 0.65 ns (−51 %) | 0.70 → 0.54 ns (−22 %) |
| #5838 | non-const `arr[i]` | 1.59 → 0.87 ns (−45 %) | 0.83 → 0.66 ns (−21 %) |
| #5838 / #5835 | `std::sort` of 1M json ints | 132 → 95 ms (−28 %) | 122 → 82 ms (−33 %) |
| #5835 | range-for over an array, per element | 2.53 → 1.27 ns (−50 %) | 1.12 → 0.96 ns (−14 %) |
| #5835 | reverse iteration, per element | 3.48 → 1.58 ns (−55 %) | 1.12 → 0.96 ns (−14 %) |
| #5835 | copy + destroy object of 100k ints | 5.75 → 3.32 ms (−42 %) | 5.18 → 3.01 ms (−42 %) |
| #5835 | `diff({}, citm)` | 3.24 → 1.50 ms (−54 %) | 5.46 → 2.17 ms (−60 %) |
| #5835 | copy + destroy citm | 1.59 → 1.50 ms (−6 %) | 2.58 → 2.19 ms (−15 %) |
| #5831 | `parse()` citm with callback | 4.21 → 3.97 ms (−6 %) | 7.00 → 6.54 ms (−7 %) |
| #5839 | `from_cbor` / `from_msgpack` / `from_ubjson` / `from_bson` citm | −4 … −7 % | −10 … −16 % |
| #5839 | `from_bjdata` twitter | 1.55 → 1.49 ms (−4 %) | 2.73 → 2.60 ms (−5 %) |
| #5842 | `patch(diff(a, b))` citm | −6.6 % (see above) | −9.5 % (see above) |

¹ The rest is `ordered_map`'s linear key lookup, not the diagnostics. Without `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` the same `update()` takes 269 ms on clang. The diagnostics overhead on top of it dropped from about 37 % to about 20 %.

**Regression guard**, parse/accept/dump on all three documents:
- **clang:** within ±2 %, except parse of citm and canada, which is about 4 % faster.
- **GCC:** within ±2 %, except parse of citm, which is 10 % faster.

**Slower on GCC, small:** `citm == citm` +3 %, `diff(citm, citm)` +4 %, `ordered_json` parse of citm with `JSON_DIAGNOSTICS` +3 %. The clang run-to-run spread on these rows is 2–8 %. #5840 describes the GCC `==` effect on large documents.

The benchmark source is standalone (one `.cpp` file, no Google Benchmark) and can be posted on request.

## Breaking changes

No breaking changes. The new helpers are in `nlohmann::detail`, and exception types, ids and messages are unchanged.
